result.reviewScopeSummary: Initial verification of Story 1 covered the story and full tech-design set, the smooth-turn runtime and persistence paths, the story/foundation tests, the story gate and epic gate, a manual reopen persistence check, and a stale-snapshot overwrite reproduction against the real file store.

newFindings.title: Whole-snapshot turn writes can erase previously generated smooth state
newFindings.evidence: `ensureSmoothTurn` rewrites the entire turn snapshot through `writeTurns` without acquiring `ThreadMutationCoordinator` or any other derived-state lease ([src/thread/async-thread/services/smooth-turn-service.ts:176-228]). `writeTurns` only guards on `thread.sourceRevision` and `messageHighWatermark`, and neither value changes when smooth state is persisted ([src/context-steward/store/file-thread-store.ts:345-363]). A real-store stale-snapshot reproduction succeeded with two writes from the same source revision and dropped the first smooth record, ending with `[ {"turnId":"turn-a"}, {"turnId":"turn-b","smoothText":"[assistant]\nB"} ]`. This breaks the guarantee that closed turns keep their deterministic smooth artifact once generated.

productionPathFindings: Derived smooth-state persistence is still vulnerable to stale-snapshot overwrite because runtime code writes the whole `turns.json` snapshot without a derived-state revision/lease that survives beyond the current in-process queue.
additionalObservations: The mapped Story 1 test file covers all 8 explicit TCs plus the decided empty/noise-only section case, and all of those tests passed.

A manual reopen check with a second `FileThreadStore` instance confirmed that the single-writer happy path does persist smooth state to `turns.json` across store reopen; the blocker is stale-write safety, not basic disk persistence.
No fake adapter, placeholder branch, or mock-only runtime path was found in the smooth-turn formatter/service itself.
